sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ever wondered how your favorite apps are made? Software development isn't just coding - it's a step-by-step journey!

• The 7 key stages of building software
• How to turn ideas into working programs
• Why going back to fix things is totally normal

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine building a treehouse. You wouldn't just start hammering wood together! First you'd:

• Ask your friends what features they want (a slide? a trapdoor?)
• Sketch a blueprint
• Gather materials
• Build it piece by piece
• Test if it's safe
• Let everyone use it
• Fix any wobbly parts later

Software development works the same way! Here's how it breaks down:

• **Requirements**: Like asking your friends what they want in the treehouse. What should the software do?
• **Analysis**: Figuring out what materials (data) you need. What goes in? What comes out?
• **Design**: Drawing the blueprint. How will all the pieces fit together?

Each stage builds on the last, but sometimes you need to go back and fix things - just like realizing you need stronger wood after testing the treehouse!

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ Software development has 7 main stages - not just coding!
✓ Requirements come first - always know what you're building
✓ IPO: Input → Process → Output is the core of every program
✓ Testing catches bugs before users see them
✓ It's okay to go back and fix things - that's normal!

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Talk to users early - don't assume what they want
Break big problems into small pieces
Test as you go - don't wait until the end
donts: Don't skip the design phase - it saves time later
Don't ignore requirements - they're your roadmap
Don't be afraid to go back and fix things
sections.protip: The best developers spend 50% of their time on requirements and design - not just coding!

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Where you see this in action:

examples.how: Uses requirements gathering to understand what features users need (transfers, bill pay), then designs secure systems before coding
Game designers create storyboards (requirements), level designers create maps (design), then programmers implement the game mechanics
Analyze customer shopping patterns (analysis), design checkout flows (design), then implement payment systems (implementation)

sections.title: 🧪 Practice Problem
sections.content: Let's build a simple tip calculator together!

problem.description: Create a program that calculates a 15% tip on a restaurant bill. The user should enter the bill amount, and the program should display the tip amount and total bill.
problem.explanation: We first get the bill amount from the user. Then we calculate 15% of that amount for the tip. Finally, we add them together for the total. The printf method helps format the output to 2 decimal places.

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 Software development is a step-by-step process - not just coding!
📌 Always start with requirements - know what you're building
📌 Break problems into small pieces (IPO: Input → Process → Output)
📌 Test early and often - catch bugs before users do
📌 You're ready to build your first complete program!
